title: Local structural properties of locally quasi-coherent flat-compatible modules
statement: Work in the universes and small-skeleton convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. For a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme] and an algebraic stack $\mathcal Z/S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], its big etale site has all objects and arrows of the fibred category in [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra], with coverings lying over jointly surjective etale scheme maps. Its structure sheaf is $\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z}(z)=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ for $z$ over $U$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For a module sheaf $M$, write $M_z=M|_{U_{\mathrm{et}}}$ for restriction to the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Call $M$ locally quasi-coherent if each $M_z$ is the associated etale sheaf of a quasi-coherent Zariski module [pqf-def-coherent], whose sections on $v:V\to U$ are $\Gamma(V,v^*M_z^{\mathrm{Zar}})$. For an arrow $a:z\to z^{\prime}$ over $u:U\to U^{\prime}$, let $c_a:u_{\mathrm{et}}^*M_{z^{\prime}}\to M_z$ be the canonical map induced by restriction and tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Call $M$ flat-compatible if $c_a$ is an isomorphism for every flat $u$ [def-weil-flat-morphism]. For each $\mathcal Z$, let $\mathcal M_{\mathcal Z}$ be the full subcategory of locally quasi-coherent flat-compatible module sheaves. Then $\mathcal M_{\mathcal Z}$ contains zero, is closed under kernels and cokernels of maps between its objects, and is closed under extensions in all big etale module sheaves. Precomposition along every morphism $h:\mathcal A\to\mathcal Z$ of algebraic stacks preserves $\mathcal M$. For every jointly surjective family of smooth morphisms $p_j:\mathcal Z_j\to\mathcal Z$, a module $M$ belongs to $\mathcal M_{\mathcal Z}$ if and only if every $p_j^*M$ belongs to $\mathcal M_{\mathcal Z_j}$. Smoothness and joint surjectivity are tested on scheme charts and field-valued objects as in [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus].

proof.text: For every flat scheme map $u:U\to U'$, the small-etale tensor pullback $u_{\mathrm{et}}^*$ is exact on all module sheaves. Indeed $u$ is flat on etale scheme charts: for etale $V\to U'$ and etale $T\to U\times_{U'}V$, the map $T\to V$ is the composite of an etale, hence flat, map with the base change of the flat map $u$, so it is flat by the base-change and composition stability and the implication etale $\Rightarrow$ flat of [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] (schemes are algebraic stacks and scheme maps are representable). Therefore [lem-sfb-space-flat-etale-ringed-comparison], applied to the schemes $U,U'$ as algebraic spaces, says that $\mathcal O_U$ is flat over $u^{-1}\mathcal O_{U'}$. The transported inverse image is exact by [lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact], and tensoring it with this flat module is exact by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Thus both functors in the formula $u_{\mathrm{et}}^*=\mathcal O_U\otimes_{u^{-1}\mathcal O_{U'}}u^{-1}(-)$ are exact. Independently, the restriction $R_z$ to each scheme test is exact by [lem-sfb-fibred-big-etale-restriction-calculus]. These exactness statements apply to arbitrary ambient modules, including kernels and the middle term of an extension before their local quasi-coherence is known.

The zero sheaf restricts to the associated zero quasi-coherent module, and every comparison on it is the unique isomorphism $0\to0$. For a map $F\to G$ in $\mathcal M_{\mathcal Z}$, put $K=\ker(F\to G)$ and $C=\operatorname{coker}(F\to G)$ in ambient big-etale modules. Exact restriction gives $R_zK=\ker(R_zF\to R_zG)$ and $R_zC=\operatorname{coker}(R_zF\to R_zG)$. The equivalence [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] identifies associated quasi-coherent Zariski modules with site quasi-coherent small-etale modules. Apply [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits] to the scheme $U$ viewed as an algebraic space. Its kernel and cokernel assertions, followed by the inverse equivalence, show that $R_zK$ and $R_zC$ are associated quasi-coherent modules for every $z$. Thus $K,C$ are locally quasi-coherent.

Fix an arrow $a:z\to z'$ over a flat $u$. Naturality of $c_a$ gives a commutative square with horizontal maps $u_{\mathrm{et}}^*R_{z'}F\to u_{\mathrm{et}}^*R_{z'}G$ and $R_zF\to R_zG$, and vertical maps $c_{a,F},c_{a,G}$, both isomorphisms. By the exactness in step 1, its induced maps on kernels and cokernels have sources $u_{\mathrm{et}}^*R_{z'}K,u_{\mathrm{et}}^*R_{z'}C$ and targets $R_zK,R_zC$. They are precisely $c_{a,K},c_{a,C}$: their kernel inclusions, respectively cokernel projections, commute by naturality, and their universal properties give uniqueness. A square whose vertical arrows are invertible induces invertible maps on kernels and cokernels, with inverse induced by the inverse square. Hence $K,C$ are flat-compatible as well.

Let $0\to F\to H\to G\to0$ be short exact in all big-etale modules, with $F,G\in\mathcal M_{\mathcal Z}$. Exactness of $R_z$ makes its restriction short exact. Using the scheme/etale quasi-coherent equivalence, [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-extension-closed] implies that $R_zH$ is associated quasi-coherent for every $z$. For each flat arrow $a$ over $u$, apply $u_{\mathrm{et}}^*R_{z'}$ and $R_z$ to this sequence. Step 1 gives two short exact rows, and naturality of $c_a$ gives a morphism of rows. Its outer arrows are $c_{a,F}$ and $c_{a,G}$, which are isomorphisms. The short five lemma [lem-weil-pbc-short-five-lemma] gives that $c_{a,H}$ is an isomorphism. This proves extension closure in the entire ambient module category.

source.place: 06WM, lemma-lqc-colimits, proof (3), in stacks-sheaves.tex; 0764, proof (2), extension argument.

proof.text: For $h:\mathcal A\to\mathcal Z$, [lem-sfb-fibred-big-etale-restriction-calculus] says that precomposition is a sheaf, $R_y(h^*M)=R_{h(y)}M$, and its comparison for $a$ is the comparison for $h(a)$. The functor $h$ lies over schemes, so these arrows have the same underlying scheme map. The first equality gives local quasi-coherence; the second gives flat-compatibility whenever that map is flat. Thus every $h^*$ preserves $\mathcal M$, and in particular membership implies membership after each $p_j^*$.

Assume every $p_j^*M$ belongs to $\mathcal M_{\mathcal Z_j}$. For every object $z$ over $U$, [lem-sfb-smooth-stack-family-etale-object-lifts] applies to the given smooth, jointly surjective family: it gives an etale covering $e_i:U_i\to U$, objects $y_i\in\mathcal Z_{j(i)}(U_i)$, and isomorphisms $p_{j(i)}(y_i)\simeq e_i^*z$. Its statement allows nonrepresentable $p_j$, arbitrary base schemes and arbitrary small families, exactly as required here. We will use these lifts first for $z$ to detect local quasi-coherence, and then for the target $z'$ of each flat arrow to detect its comparison isomorphism.

source.place: 075Y, lemma-check-lqc-on-etale-covering, proof first paragraph; 0764, proof (3), smooth atlas reduction and local lifts (06XH).

proof.text: Apply step 6 to $z$ over $U$. For each lifted $y_i$ over $U_i$ in some $\mathcal Z_j$, the restriction of $R_zM$ to $(U_i)_{\mathrm{et}}$ identifies with $R_{y_i}(p_j^*M)$ by the etale-arrow and precomposition assertions of [lem-sfb-fibred-big-etale-restriction-calculus]. It is associated quasi-coherent by hypothesis, so it is site quasi-coherent by [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. Quasi-coherence on a site is local: for an object $W\to U$, pull back the covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ to $W$ and then choose the local free presentations from [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] on each member; composing these coverings gives the requisite local presentations on $W$. Thus $R_zM$ is site quasi-coherent, and the inverse equivalence makes it associated to a quasi-coherent Zariski module. As $z$ was arbitrary, $M$ is locally quasi-coherent.

source.place: 075Y, proof, final paragraph; spaces-properties.tex 03M0, lemma-characterize-quasi-coherent, local presentation argument.

proof.text:
For a flat arrow $a:z\to z'$ over $u:U\to U'$, choose the etale lifts $e_i':U_i'\to U'$ of $z'$ from step 6, into $\mathcal Z_{j(i)}$. Put $U_i=U\times_{U'}U_i'$, with $e_i:U_i\to U$ and $u_i:U_i\to U_i'$. The family $\{e_i\}$ is an etale cover, and $u_i$ is flat by base change [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. Pulling back each lifted object gives an arrow $a_i$ of $\mathcal Z_{j(i)}$ over $u_i$. Its comparison for $p_{j(i)}^*M$ is invertible by hypothesis. Let $r_i:z_i\to z$ and $r_i':z_i'\to z'$ be the etale arrows. In $\mathcal Z$ one has $a r_i=r_i'p_{j(i)}(a_i)$. The composition identity of [lem-sfb-fibred-big-etale-restriction-calculus] therefore gives
$$c_{r_i,M}\,e_i^*c_{a,M}=c_{p_{j(i)}(a_i),M}\,u_i^*c_{r_i',M}.$$
Here the canonical pullback-composition identifications are understood; both $c_{r_i,M}$ and $c_{r_i',M}$ are invertible, and precomposition identifies the other comparison with that of $p_{j(i)}^*M$. Hence each $e_i^*c_{a,M}$ is invertible. Etale pullback is restriction to the slice by the same calculus. Invertibility is local for sheaves: the local inverses agree on overlaps because they invert the same map, and the sheaf gluing axiom produces its unique inverse. Consequently $c_{a,M}$ is invertible. This holds for every flat $a$, so $M$ is flat-compatible. Together with step 7 and the forward implication of step 5 this proves smooth-cover detection.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q25-5f26397b7 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, both new nodes, every cited statement and the parent's use of the item, and checked them against Stacks 06WL, 06WM(1)-(3), 075D(1)-(4) with equation-comparison-modules, 06XH(2), 075Y and 0764(1)-(3), proofs included. The statement matches the sources clause by clause and adds no finiteness hypotheses. Steps 2-8 are correct. Step 2 (kernels/cokernels) applies the space qcoh lemma to the scheme U, whose small etale site is U_et. Step 4 (extensions) uses the extension lemma, which allows an arbitrary middle term, and the short five lemma. Step 8 (flat-comparison detection) rests on the 075D(1) composition identity; I checked its order, and r_i exists by the fibred-groupoid property. One repairable fault, E1/C4: step 1 used lem-sfb-space-flat-etale-ringed-comparison, which assumes chart-flatness, for a flat scheme map without deriving it. The FIX adds that two-line derivation (base change, composition, etale implies flat) and cites lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus, already in proof_deps. Nothing else changed. New node lem-sfb-fibred-big-etale-restriction-calculus is true: it is 075D in module form plus exactness of R_z and the sheaf property of precomposition. New node lem-sfb-smooth-stack-family-etale-object-lifts is true by atlas reduction and 06XH(2)/0CFV. Both nodes are statement-only and self-contained, with three kinds of search recorded. rg -L over the DAG found no duplicates: the fppf inverse-image, representable smooth-space section, atlas-descent and fppf-qcoh restriction nodes all have different conclusions. Neither new node restates an item clause. Accepted tool uses: lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence and lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact, both generic. Batch-5: every listed citation is a definition (def-trf-algebraic-space, def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism, def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module) or a generic topos/qcoh tool, none of them part of the trace formula or Poincare duality or their proofs.
